prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: Link Inventory Audit — Q1 2025 (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "Page title" · longest unbreakable unit 100px · widest one-line content 319px
  col 2: header "URL" · longest unbreakable unit 324px · widest one-line content 841px
  col 3: header "Last checked" · longest unbreakable unit 61px · widest one-line content 96px
  col 4: header "Status code" · longest unbreakable unit 47px · widest one-line content 86px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 720px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 720px wide (column widths sum to at most 719px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 720px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"Audit a set of links by identifying each page, its destination, when it was checked, and the resulting status code.","tasks":["Find a page by title and trace across its row to its URL, check date, and status.","Scan status codes to locate links that may need attention.","Compare check dates to identify stale results.","Read or verify a URL against its page title."],"relations":["Each row binds one page title to one URL, one check date, and one status code.","The date qualifies the status as the result of a particular check."],"roles":["Page titles identify entries; URLs identify their destinations.","Dates and status codes are compact audit results that support vertical scanning.","Headers name the four fields; all six body rows have the same structural role."],"keep_whole":["Individual words, date components, and status codes.","URL components where wrapping opportunities permit, especially the host and meaningful path segments."],"may_wrap":["Page titles at word boundaries.","URLs at available URL break opportunities; long destinations will need multiple lines.","Multiword headers when the space is better used for body content."],"same_scale":["All page titles share one column scale, and all URLs share another.","The two audit-result columns should both remain compact and easy to scan, though their widths need not be equal."],"h_vs_v":"The URL needs the largest share of the width, but giving it more space makes titles or audit fields taller. Extra row height is acceptable when it preserves readable titles, recognizable URL segments, and scannable results."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d1r3A, d1r3B, d1r3C, d1r2A.
Measured facts:
d1r3A: column widths [175, 360, 100, 84] px · table 720×580 px · row heights [60, 106, 106, 60, 83, 83, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 2/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
d1r3B: column widths [165, 368, 105, 81] px · table 720×580 px · row heights [60, 83, 106, 83, 83, 83, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 2/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
d1r3C: column widths [175, 337, 100, 107] px · table 720×580 px · row heights [60, 106, 106, 60, 83, 83, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 1/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 1 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
d1r2A: column widths [175, 343, 117, 84] px · table 720×580 px · row heights [60, 106, 106, 60, 83, 83, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 1/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). Then either propose up to 3 improved designs (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or try an important unexplored idea) or, if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement, set "done": true. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
